summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist. He served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

A. Charles Muller specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Stony Brook University (1988) and studied at the University of Virginia. He held professorships at Toyo Gakuen University (~1997–2008) and the University of Tokyo (~2008–2019).

A. H. Armstrong was a philosopher who studied at Jesus College (~1928–1932). He held posts at Swansea University (~1936–1939), the University of Malta (~1939–1943), Cardiff University (~1946–1950), and the University of Liverpool (~1950–1972).

A. K. Ramanujan was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, the University of Mysore, and Indiana University. He held academic posts at Baroda College, the University of Chicago (~1962–1993), and Harvard University (~1987–1988).

A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist. He served as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin (attested 1942) and held a post at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1942).
A. N. Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Ralph Lilley Turner (attested 1941) and held a post at the University of Mysore.

A. V. Williams Jackson specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Washburn Hopkins, later serving on Columbia University's faculty (~1886–1891 and ~1895–1935).
A. W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and held an academic post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).

Aaron P. Proffitt is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He earned degrees from the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Michigan (PhD ~2008–2015, supervised by Micah L. Auerback), joining the University at Albany, SUNY as assistant professor around 2015.

Abdur Rehman is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Michel Bréal (~1867–1870) and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877) and the University of Paris (~1885–1888).

Abigail I. MacBain specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008), where she studied under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and Shayne Clarke, among others.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his MA under David P. Jackson and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen, later working as a research associate at LMU Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at LMU Munich, later holding an academic post at the University of Göttingen (~1874–1880).
Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1833–1837). He served as Direktor of the Köllnisches Gymnasium from ~1870 to 1881.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Greg Bailey (attested 2004) and served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).
Adam Hardy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at The Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe, and held an academic post at Cardiff University around 2003.

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche, and later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.
